## Historical audit — H0206

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane5/codex_parallel_12_lane5_B_r1/infer_logs/sqlfmt-create-table-ddl-formatting/turn_1/trajs.json`. Event references below are to this file; offsets are half-open character ranges in the supplied observations.

**Inferred goal:** Add CREATE TABLE DDL formatting, apparently on a branch from `main`. The original task specification is not visible, so the precise required formatting and scope cannot be established from the task name or the student’s expectation alone.

| Area | Evidence and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Actual change | The student created `ddl-formatting` from `main` (main agent events 4–5, [0,768) and [0,5592)). Later status/diff output showed no source changes, and the student reported no commit (events 61–62, [0,743) and [0,642); event 71, [0,739)). The supplied inventory records a zero-byte patch. |
| Autonomous exploration | The student read formatter, analyzer, token, rule and node-management code; inspected dispatch and existing tests; and probed tokenization. The sample CREATE TABLE body appeared as a single `DATA` token under the normal analyzer (events 24–25, [0,1044) and [0,1498)). A separate CORE-only probe produced individual name, bracket and comma tokens (events 63–64, [0,1128) and [0,2124)). The inspected unsupported-DDL rule routes matching statements to the unsupported ruleset (event 54, [0,8760)). These observations support a task-specific diagnosis, not a tested fix. |
| Visible validation | A formatter call returned the sample unchanged (events 16 and 20, [0,832) and [0,516)). A student-authored expected-output assertion failed against that unchanged output (events 44–45, [0,1066) and [0,905)); its expected layout is not independently established as the specification. No post-fix verification was possible because no fix was made; the student reported no verification tests run (event 71). |
| Teacher input | The inventory lists shared hint files as available, but supplies neither their contents nor a captured delivered hint or system-prompt text. Thus actual teacher input and student adoption are **not established**; availability is not receipt. |
| Outcome | The supplied inventory reports **empty patch, formally not solved**, with fail-to-pass 0/32 and pass-to-pass 1273/1273. These are reported evaluation counts, not evidence of a successful implementation. The trace ended normally with an explicit incomplete-work report; it does not establish a technical interruption or failure of an implemented algorithm (top-level metadata, [0,2456); event 71). |

**Lessons and uncertainty:** Transferably, reproducing a failure and inspecting dispatch and token representation can distinguish untouched input from downstream formatting behavior; reproduction alone is not a delivered solution. Here, the relationship between unsupported-DDL dispatch and `DATA` preservation is supported by the inspected code and probes, but whether a particular dispatch or formatting change would satisfy the unseen specification, preserve other DDL forms, and pass safety checks remains untested. Why the student stopped before implementation is unknown.
